requirement_text: Only the candidates whose eligibility is defined in the 'Principles Governing International Student Admissions' drawn up by the Council of Higher Education can apply to these quotas.
limitations: REFERENCE, NOT A RULE. METU's 'Who can Apply?' page states no eligibility criterion of its own - it delegates entirely to YÖK's Principles. A pipeline that scrapes this page and finds no criteria would conclude METU has no international eligibility requirements. It has all of them, by reference.
researcher_notes: CONFIRMS AND SHARPENS the earlier finding that METU states none of its own rules. The applicable clauses - including the nested exclusions - are the YÖK Esaslar rows already captured in requirements_batch9_yok-esaslar (REQ-8001 onward). Those rows are METU's eligibility rules. This row is the pointer that binds them. Contrast Istanbul Technical University (REQ-9110 onward), which restates the same YÖK categories in full on its own page.

requirement_text: IELTS exams taken on or after the 24th of December 2022 will not be anymore accepted.
limitations: Read the direction of this rule carefully: it excludes RECENT certificates, not old ones. It is the inverse of every other validity rule in this corpus, all of which expire OLD scores. Any evaluator that models test recency as a single max-age constraint will get METU exactly backwards and tell a student their fresh 2026 IELTS qualifies.
researcher_notes: HIGH-IMPACT EXCLUSION. IELTS is the default English test for ORYN's UK-oriented Turkish students; a student holding IELTS 8.0 from 2025 cannot use it at METU at all. Effectively METU no longer accepts IELTS, since every currently-valid certificate postdates 24 December 2022. The page still lists IELTS among accepted tests, so the exclusion and the acceptance sit on the same page - exactly the storage hazard is_exclusion exists for.

requirement_text: Exam results such as TR-YÖS, SAT, QUDURAT, and TQDK are valid for two years. Documents holding the status of a high-school diploma are valid with any date.
limitations: RECENCY RULE with a per-qualification-type split in a single sentence: two years for exams, unlimited for diplomas. A per-institution max-age field cannot hold both halves.
researcher_notes: Fourth institution in this corpus with a per-qualification-type validity window, after Koc, Edinburgh and Exeter. Two of the four are Turkish and two British, so this is a general admissions pattern rather than a national quirk. The 'such as' is doing real work: the list is illustrative, not closed, so a student's exam not named here has an unstated validity window.

requirement_text: The criteria specified in this list represent the minimum application requirements. However, fulfilling these requirements does not guarantee admission. Admission and rejection decisions are made in line with the quotas announced for the program, based on a holistic evaluation of additional data and documents that the applicant submitted.
limitations: Not evaluable, and deliberately so. Recorded because ORYN's Requirement Check must not render a student who clears every METU threshold as admitted or likely admitted. METU says in its own words that clearing the thresholds is a floor for consideration, not an outcome.
researcher_notes: Directly relevant to non-negotiable 13 (application readiness is not admission probability). The institution itself supplies the disclaimer, so ORYN can cite rather than assert it.

requirement_text: Applicants must be in their final year of high school or have already graduated.
limitations: text_fidelity is extracted_summary; only the phrase 'in their final year of high school or have already graduated' survived extraction as a quotation.
researcher_notes: Directly relevant to ORYN's 14-18 user base: a 16-year-old cannot apply, and the product should say so rather than surfacing ITU as an open target.

requirement_text: Foreign nationals who have not attended Turkish secondary education, with specific exceptions for embassy and international schools.
limitations: text_fidelity is extracted_summary and the nested exceptions were compressed by the extraction step. The AUTHORITATIVE text of this rule is YÖK's, captured verbatim in Turkish at REQ-2026-08-21-8001 in requirements_batch9_yok-esaslar, which carries the depth-2 carve-out (embassy schools / MOBIS international private schools / MEB-or-YOK project students) in full. Evaluate against the YÖK row, not this one.
researcher_notes: ITU RESTATES YÖK's eligibility categories on its own page rather than only linking to them - the opposite editorial choice from METU (REQ-9101). Both are correct; a scraper that treats page-presence as rule-presence would wrongly conclude ITU is stricter than METU. Recorded to make the restatement-vs-reference distinction visible in the data.

requirement_text: Turkish citizens who have completed all of their secondary education (high school) in a foreign country
limitations: The word 'all' is load-bearing and is the exclusion in disguise: a Turkish citizen who completed most but not all of high school abroad is NOT eligible under this route. YÖK's own text at REQ-8001 onward carries the precise formulation.
researcher_notes: This route matters commercially for ORYN: Turkish-passport students at international schools abroad are a core segment, and whether they enter via YKS or via the international quota turns entirely on this clause.

requirement_text: It is not possible to apply with any other exams or test scores lower than those presented.
limitations: CLOSED-LIST EXCLUSION. The accepted-exam list is exhaustive, not illustrative - contrast METU's 'exams such as' (REQ-9103). A student holding a qualification absent from ITU's list is ineligible, which a requirement store holding only positive thresholds cannot express: it has no row to fail against.
researcher_notes: The list itself is published in a per-cycle announcement PDF that could not be retrieved (see the blocked-institutions list in this batch's report). The closed-list RULE is recorded here even though its contents are not, because the rule changes how a missing match must be interpreted.

requirement_text: An English Proficiency test result accepted by ITU Senate need to be submitted during registration.
limitations: Required at REGISTRATION, not at application - a different deadline from the application deadline, and one ORYN's deadline engine has no row for. Students without a valid score take a one-year English Preparatory Course rather than being rejected, so failing this is not a disqualification.
researcher_notes: The prep-year consequence is why this must not evaluate to not_met. It is a met / met-with-preparatory-year outcome, a third state the evaluator does not currently have.

limitations: TOEFL iBT, legacy 0-120 scale, correctly bounded by ITU to tests taken before the 21 January 2026 ETS rescale. The defect is what is MISSING: no post-cutover 1-6 row appeared in the extraction, and the page's own last-updated stamp is 08.07.2021 (University Senate Decision No. 776) with amendments logged to 2023. If ITU has genuinely not published a 1-6 threshold, a student sitting TOEFL today has NO applicable ITU rule at all - neither met nor not_met. Confirm against the rendered page before ingesting; the extraction may have dropped a row.
researcher_notes: First institution in this corpus whose TOEFL problem is an ABSENCE rather than a stale number. Manchester publishes an undated legacy threshold; ITU publishes a correctly dated legacy threshold and appears to publish no successor. Both leave a current test-taker unevaluable, by opposite routes.

requirement_text: TOEFL IBT Special Home Edition exam results will not be accepted as of the Spring Semester
limitations: 'as of the Spring Semester' names no year in the quoted clause; the page attributes it to Senate Decision 808 dated 27.07.2022, which places the effective semester in the 2022-2023 academic year. Recorded without synthesising the year into the requirement text.
researcher_notes: EXCLUSION on delivery mode. Third distinct home-edition policy in this batch: Bath accepts iBT Home Edition, Liverpool rejects it, ITU rejects it by Senate decision. A shared accepted-tests lookup is wrong for at least one of the three.

requirement_text: TOEFL iBT and PTE Academic exam results must be taken from the exam centers in state universities
limitations: EXCLUSION ON TEST VENUE - a dimension no score field in ORYN carries. A student with TOEFL iBT 100 taken at a private test centre holds a fully qualifying score that ITU rejects. Page attributes it to Senate Decision 838 (06.07.2023), effective from the 2023-2024 academic year.
researcher_notes: Fourth distinct provenance dimension found across this corpus, after score type (Koc superscore), retake type (Edinburgh One Skill Retake), delivery mode (Bath/Liverpool/ITU home edition) and now venue. Together these are the argument for storing an excluded-provenance list on the rule rather than a bare threshold.

requirement_text: 55 – 74 / 90 (Before the start of the 2026–2027 fall semester)
limitations: PTE Academic, bounded by a SUNSET rather than a start date: valid only before the 2026-2027 fall semester begins. That semester begins within weeks of the 2026-08-21 retrieval date, so this threshold is on the point of expiring and no successor row was captured. Re-check before ingesting; ingesting it as a live rule would tell a student a PTE score qualifies days after it stops qualifying.
researcher_notes: The only forward-dated expiry found in this corpus. It is also the reason a requirement store needs a validity window on the RULE, not only on the student's certificate - this rule expires, independently of any score's age.
